stem:
Hypophosphorous acid is an inorganic acid.

The conjugate base of hypophosphorous acid is $\text{H}_2\text{PO}_2^-$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Give the formula of hypophosphorous acid.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
$\text{H}_2\text{PO}_2^-$ is a strong reducing agent. It can be used to reduce metal cations without the need for electrolysis.

equation 1 $$\text{HPO}_3^{2-} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} + 2\text{e}^- \rightleftharpoons \text{H}_2\text{PO}_2^- + 3\text{OH}^-$$ $E^\ominus = -1.57\text{ V}$

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text:
In an experiment, an alkaline $\text{HPO}_3^{2-}/\text{H}_2\text{PO}_2^-$ half-cell is constructed with $[\text{H}_2\text{PO}_2^-] = 0.050\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$.

All other ions are at their standard concentration.

Predict how the value of $E$ of this half-cell differs from its $E^\ominus$ value.

Explain your answer.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
The $\text{Cr}^{3+}/\text{Cr}$ half-cell has a standard electrode potential of $-0.74\text{ V}$.

An electrochemical cell consists of an alkaline $\text{HPO}_3^{2-}/\text{H}_2\text{PO}_2^-$ half-cell and a $\text{Cr}^{3+}/\text{Cr}$ half-cell.

Calculate the standard cell potential, $E^\ominus_{\text{cell}}$.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text:
Complete the diagram in Fig. 2.1 to show how the standard electrode potential of the $\text{Cr}^{3+}/\text{Cr}$ half-cell can be measured relative to that of the standard hydrogen electrode.

Identify the chemicals, conditions and relevant pieces of apparatus.

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}

Fig. 2.1

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.text:
Label Fig. 2.1 to show:

- which is the positive electrode
- the direction of electron flow in the external circuit.

parts.label: (b)(v)
parts.text:
$\text{H}_2\text{PO}_2^-$ reduces $\text{Ni}^{2+}$ to $\text{Ni}$ in alkaline conditions.

Use equation 1 to construct the ionic equation for this reaction.

equation 1 $$\text{HPO}_3^{2-} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} + 2\text{e}^- \rightleftharpoons \text{H}_2\text{PO}_2^- + 3\text{OH}^-$$

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
$\text{H}_2\text{PO}_2^-\text{(aq)}$ reacts with $\text{OH}^-\text{(aq)}$.

$$\text{H}_2\text{PO}_2^-\text{(aq)} + \text{OH}^-\text{(aq)} \rightarrow \text{HPO}_3^{2-}\text{(g)} + \text{H}_2\text{(g)}$$

Table 2.1 shows the results of a series of experiments used to investigate the rate of this reaction.

Table 2.1

| experiment | $[\text{H}_2\text{PO}_2^-\text{(aq)}]$ $/\text{mol dm}^{-3}$ | $[\text{OH}^-\text{(aq)}]$ $/\text{mol dm}^{-3}$ | volume of $\text{H}_2$ produced in 60 s $/\text{cm}^3$ |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | 0.40 | 2.00 | 6.4 |
| 2 | 0.80 | 2.00 | 12.8 |
| 3 | 1.20 | 1.00 | 4.8 |

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text:
The volume of $\text{H}_2$ was measured under room conditions.

Use the molar volume of gas, $V_{\text{m}}$, and the data from experiment 1 to calculate the rate of reaction in $\text{mol dm}^{-3}\text{ s}^{-1}$.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
The rate equation was found to be:

$$\text{rate} = k [\text{H}_2\text{PO}_2^-\text{(aq)}] [\text{OH}^-\text{(aq)}]^2$$

Show that the data in Table 2.1 is consistent with the rate equation.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text: State the units of the rate constant, $k$, for the reaction.

parts.label: (c)(iv)
parts.text:
The experiment is repeated using a large excess of $\text{OH}^-\text{(aq)}$.

Under these conditions, the rate equation is:

$$\text{rate} = k_1 [\text{H}_2\text{PO}_2^-\text{(aq)}]$$

$k_1 = 8.25 \times 10^{-5}\text{ s}^{-1}$

Calculate the value of the half-life, $t_{\frac{1}{2}}$, of the reaction.

parts.label: (c)(v)
parts.text: Describe how an increase in temperature affects the value of the rate constant, $k_1$.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
A student suggests that the reaction between $\text{H}_2\text{PO}_2^-\text{(aq)}$ and $\text{OH}^-\text{(aq)}$ might happen more quickly in the presence of a heterogeneous catalyst.

Describe the mode of action of a heterogeneous catalyst.
